topics.label: Introduction to the initiation and resolution of inflammation
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the lecture topic, framing the session as an integration of previously introduced immune mechanisms and cell types.

topics.label: Mechanisms and requirements of innate immune recognition
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish how the innate immune system distinguishes self from non-self by sensing pathogen- and damage-associated molecular patterns through germline-encoded receptors.

topics.label: Pattern recognition receptor families, signaling, and inflammasome activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail major pattern recognition receptor families, their subcellular signaling cascades, and the inflammasome complex that processes inflammatory cytokines.

topics.label: Leukocyte recruitment, trafficking, and systemic inflammatory responses
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how activated sentinel cells orchestrate leukocyte extravasation into tissues, lymphatic drainage to lymph nodes, and potential systemic outcomes such as septic shock.

topics.label: Resolution of inflammation, tissue repair, and chronic inflammatory adaptations
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how acute inflammation is resolved, how tissues are repaired, and how chronic inflammation and granulomas develop when resolution fails.
